intro: Thailand stretches from forested northern mountains to the beaches and islands of the far south, with the rice-growing plains of the Chao Phraya river in between.

chapters.title: Four regions
text: The north is mountainous and cooler; Doi Inthanon is the highest peak at 2,565 m. The north-east, called Isan, is a dry plateau bordered by the Mekong. The central plains around Bangkok are fertile rice land.
The south is a long, narrow peninsula with the Andaman Sea on one side and the Gulf of Thailand on the other.

chapters.title: Islands and coasts
text: Phuket, Koh Samui, Koh Phi Phi and hundreds of other islands draw visitors from around the world. Limestone cliffs at Krabi and Phang Nga Bay rise out of the sea.

chapters.title: Climate
text: Thailand is tropical, with a hot season, a rainy season from about May to October and a cooler dry season. Floods in 2011 swamped parts of Bangkok.
